subject: Helios VPC — physical storage, snapshots, and deletion evidence request
messages:
From: Sara Klein <sara.klein@helios-med.com>

Cc: procurement@helios-med.com, cloud-ops@helios-med.com

Subject: Private VPC: storage location, backups & deletion evidence

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the demo last week — Helios is close to a decision but we have a couple of final compliance questions before procurement signs off. We're evaluating the private VPC offering and need clarity on three items: physical residency of customer data, snapshot/backup replication behavior, and how Redwood can provide verifiable evidence that data was deleted upon request.

Specific asks:
- Where are persistent volumes and object storage for a Private deployment physically located (granular by region)? Do we control the storage account/namespace or does Redwood own it?
- If we request a tenant deletion, what artifacts can you provide to show snapshots/backups were removed (timestamps, signed audit logs, chain-of-custody)?
- Are there any automated cross-region replication or cold backups we cannot opt out of? We need assurances that Helios data will not leave the US region unless explicitly configured.

We'd prefer short, concrete answers we can send to our legal/compliance team. If you have a standard attestation or an example deletion certificate, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Klein
Director, IT Compliance
Helios Medical
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Klein <sara.klein@helios-med.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Private VPC: storage location, backups & deletion evidence

Sara — thanks, great questions. Below is a concise breakdown for Helios's Private/VPC deployment. I attached our VPC control reference with a diagram of the default data flows.

Short answers up front:
- Physical location: Persistent volumes and object buckets for Private deployments live in a customer-dedicated storage account that is provisioned in your selected cloud region (for the US we provision in the US-WEST-2 or US-EAST-1 region per customer choice). The storage account/namespace will be created using your cloud tenancy when you select the 'customer-managed storage' option; Redwood does not retain ownership of that storage namespace in that configuration.

- Deletion evidence: We produce signed audit logs (SHA256) for lifecycle events (tenant delete, snapshot delete, object delete) and can provide a deletion certificate containing timestamps, affected resource IDs, and logs signed by our service signing key. For Private deployments we can optionally configure the signing key to be backed by your KMS/HSM so the attestations reference tenant-controlled key material.

- Replication/backups: By default we DO NOT enable cross-region replication for Private deployments unless you request multi-region DR. Automated snapshots are stored by default in the same region; cold backups are held for a configurable retention window (default 30 days). You can set retention to 0 and opt out of snapshot lifecycle policies to minimize retained copies.

More details and notes:
- Caching: ephemeral in-memory caches (LLM KV caches) are transient and removed on instance shutdown; we can configure a max TTL of 24 hours and surface cache purge events in the audit log.
- Snapshots: periodic block snapshots are created by the orchestration layer; they are namespaced under your storage account and marked as tenant-owned when customer-managed storage is selected. Snapshot deletion will trigger an asynchronous GC; we log both the deletion request and the final removal with timestamps.
- Key management: we support customer-managed KMS for encrypting at-rest volumes. If you enable CMK, snapshot metadata references only ciphertext we can't decrypt; the attestation will include the CMK key id and the fact that it was used.
- Access: Redwood operators do not have a standing path to read tenant persistent volumes in a customer-managed storage configuration; any debugging access is auditable and requires elevated approval.

Attachments: redwood-vpc-control-reference.pdf (high-level controls), helios-network-diagram.png (example overlay).

If you want, Marissa (cc) can coordinate a short call with our security engineering team to review the attestation format.

Best,
Alex
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Alex — that is helpful, thank you. A few follow-ups from our security team:

1) For the deletion certificate, can Redwood include the SHA256 of the deleted snapshot objects and a signed timestamp? Our auditors want a verifiable chain.
2) On KMS: we'd like to use our AWS KMS CMK for volumes and ensure that Redwood cannot re-encrypt snapshots without access to the CMK. Is that supported?
3) Cold backups: if we set retention to 0, is there any asynchronous replication (e.g., provider-level snapshots, cross-region cold copy) that could leave copies for longer than our retention window? We need an explicit guarantee.

Also, procurement asks whether you have a template attestation letter or if you can produce a one-off signed attestation for Helios. We can have our legal team share a short template.

Thanks — Sara

Sara — thanks for the clear asks and sorry for the slight delay. Quick summary and commitments from Redwood: please see the attached draft attestation (attestation-helios-vpc-20260828.pdf).

Commitments:
- Storage ownership: We will provision the Private deployment using Helios's cloud tenancy and customer-managed storage by default. That storage namespace will be considered tenant-owned.
- CMK: We support AWS KMS customer-managed CMKs for volume encryption. If Helios enables CMK, Redwood will not have the ability to re-encrypt snapshots without the CMK; snapshot metadata will reference the CMK key ID.
- Deletion evidence: We will provide a deletion certificate that includes the resource IDs, SHA256 hashes of deleted snapshot objects, and RFC3339 timestamps. Certificates are signed by our infra signing key. If requested, we can chain the signature to a key wrapped by Helios's KMS (i.e., attestations that include a reference to the customer key id).
- Replication/backups: For Private deployments, there is no automatic cross-region replication unless explicitly enabled for DR. Setting snapshot retention to 0 will prevent periodic snapshot retention; provider-level ephemeral snapshots are not retained beyond the configured retention. We will include the final GC timestamp in the deletion certificate.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached draft attestation and send any redline language from legal.
2) If you want the attestation signed with a Helios-referenced key, confirm the KMS key ARN we should reference.
3) If acceptable, we will produce the signed certificate within 5 business days after legal sign-off.

If helpful, Karthik (cc) can join your security call to go through the attestation fields.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
